# BetterTogether Runtime Test Suite — Final Design

## Purpose & scope

**Runtime correctness** here means the OMP-as-oracle differential invariant (Contract §1) holds when an `Application` is driven through the **real concurrent executor** — the `pipeline_common.hpp` `worker()` loop, the `SPSCQueue` handoff ring, and the `bm_gen_log_common.hpp` multi-thread spawn — where chunks of stages run on **different processing units concurrently** and hand `AppData` pointers between SPSC queues.

Today every test calls a single `dispatch_stage` on one fresh `AppData` and compares its `_out` to its golden. **Zero** tests spin up >1 worker thread, **zero** assert affinity, **zero** exercise concurrent CPU+GPU writes to adjacent buffers. The two hardest historical bugs — §1 (CUDA managed-mem partial visibility, `concurrentManagedAccess=0`) and §7 (Mali `HOST_CACHED` non-coherent stale reads) — are exactly the concurrent-memory-visibility family, and both were caught only by the sequential oracle or by hand. This suite closes that gap.

### Two load-bearing corrections to the original oracle (fold these in everywhere)

The original design's per-item self-golden oracle has two structural blind spots flagged at **high** severity across all three critiques. Both are corrected globally in this design and are **non-negotiable**:

1. **Items must be distinguishable.** If every pooled `AppData` computes the *same* golden from the *same* seed `114514`, all pool items are byte-identical, so a wrong-item write (pool aliasing, stale mapped pointer surviving `reset()`, `invalidate_all()` pulling a neighbor's buffer) writes a *correct* value into the *wrong* item and the check `a._out == a.golden` still passes.
   → **Fix:** seed each pool item `i` with `114514 + i`, carry an `item_id` through the pipeline, and assert **output id == input id** per item — not merely "output is a valid tree."

2. **Assert on what crossed the final queue edge, not on the static pool vector.** The original asserts on "EVERY pooled `AppData`," which is invariant under item drop/recycle/staleness. A never-pipelined orphan passes because its `_out` may coincidentally already hold its golden; an idempotent recompute hides a skipped write on cycle N because the buffer still holds the (identical) correct value from cycle N-1.
   → **Fix:** instrument the **last chunk's worker** to record each completed item's `get_uid()`/`item_id` into a thread-safe sink; assert the multiset of completions == exactly `kNumToProcess` **and** every one of the `kPoolSize` distinct pool objects appears ≥1 time. Additionally **poison** `_out` to a sentinel (`0xDEAD`) at the **start of each cycle** and **stamp a per-cycle execution counter** so a skipped/partial write fails the compare even on recycle.

### Harness deliverable

Extract the run-the-ring logic currently trapped inside `bt_gen_log::run_schedule()`/`warmup()` (`pipe/bm_gen_log_common.hpp` lines ~36–69) into a gtest-callable, backend-templated header **`builtin-apps/pipeline/pipeline_test_executor.hpp`**:

```cpp
template<class AppDataT, class DispatcherT, class QueueT, class OmpDispatch>
void run_pipeline(const Schedule& sched, size_t pool_size, size_t n_items,
                  OmpDispatch omp_dispatch,
                  std::function<void(AppDataT&)> per_item_check);
```

It is the harness every later category reuses by swapping the `Schedule`/Runner. **Three fixes are baked into the harness itself** (so every category inherits them rather than the original bugs):

- **SPSC fill correctness.** The producer loop `for i<kPoolSize: queues[0].enqueue(...)` drops the last item because `SPSCQueue` usable capacity is `Size-1` (one slot reserved to disambiguate full/empty). The harness must **size the queue to the next power-of-two above `kPoolSize`** and **assert every `enqueue()` returned `true`** so the full pool is actually in flight.
- **Watchdog.** `worker()` busy-yields forever on `dequeue`/`enqueue`. The harness wraps the join in a hard **30s wall-clock watchdog** (`std::async` the join); on timeout it FAILS with per-chunk enqueue/dequeue counters dumped, so a deadlock localizes to a chunk instead of a generic CI timeout.
- **Atomic `next_uid`.** `BaseAppData::next_uid` is a plain non-atomic `static uint32_t` incremented inside `reset()` on a worker thread. Make it `std::atomic<uint32_t>` with `fetch_add` (one-line fix in `base_appdata.hpp`) so the moment the harness is reused for two concurrent pipelines the uid-keyed invariants stay sound.

## Category 1 — E2E pipeline differential through the real concurrent worker/SPSC ring

**Bug class caught:** dropped-stage scheduler bugs; cross-chunk visibility gaps; pool-reuse corruption; SPSC handoff loss/dup; any non-handoff memory-ordering assumption; orphaned/starved/duplicated items.
**Backends:** OMP, CUDA, Vulkan.
**Priority:** **P0** · **Effort:** M

> The OMP-only pc cases are the cheapest, highest-coverage, locally-verifiable entry point — one test re-exercises the `worker()` loop, the `SPSCQueue` release/acquire handoff, `AppData` pool reuse, OMP→OMP cross-tier barrier visibility, and affinity-pinned dispatch, none of which has any automated coverage today. **But** note the critique: on TSO x86 OMP→OMP, the implicit barrier ending `#pragma omp parallel` makes producer writes globally visible before `enqueue`, so this path is **insensitive to handoff ordering** and must **not** be treated as the ordering gate. Ordering correctness is gated on GPU targets only (Category 3).

### Case 1.1 — OMP 2-chunk (big|little) tree e2e == per-item self-golden  *(the POC, implement first)*
- **Asserts:** Drive `Schedule { {kOMP,1,4,kBigCore}, {kOMP,5,7,kLittleCore} }` through the real ring over `kPoolSize` distinct-seeded `AppData` for `kNumToProcess` items.
  - For every item that **crossed the final queue edge**: `tree::testing::CheckStage7(a)` passes — `ExactEqual` for `s2/s3/s4/s5/s6` + `node_mask`; `NearEqual(1e-5,1e-6)` for `corner`/`cell_size`; `CheckStage7Topology` for internal octree edges.
  - **id-of-output == id-of-input** per item (distinguishable-pool oracle).
  - Multiset of last-chunk completions == exactly `kNumToProcess`; every one of the `kPoolSize` pool objects appears ≥1.
  - `_out` poisoned `0xDEAD` at start of each cycle; subset-zero detector: no item's `u_oct_child_node_mask_s7_out` is all-zero/partially-zero.
  - Per-cycle execution counter on each chunk == expected passes (idempotent-recompute staleness defeated).
  - No worker logged a throw; watchdog did not fire.
- **GATE:**
  ```
  cmake --preset pc && cmake --build --preset pc --target test-pipeline-e2e-omp \
    && ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-e2e-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc (big 0-7, little 8-23)
  ```

### Case 1.2 — OMP per-stage chunking (7 single-stage chunks, alternating big/little) tree e2e
- **Asserts:** Same harness/oracle as 1.1; `Schedule` = 7 single-stage OMP chunks alternating tier → deepest ring (7 queues, 7 worker threads), maximal cross-chunk OMP-barrier handoffs. All distinguishable-id + completion-count + execution-counter + subset-zero asserts hold.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-e2e-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 1.3 — Negative control: relaxed-ordering SPSC still passes on pc (proves pc is NOT the ordering gate)
- **Asserts:** Build a harness variant with the SPSC store/load forced to `memory_order_relaxed`; assert the OMP e2e test **still passes**. This documents that the OMP barrier masks handoff ordering and that ordering correctness must be gated on GPU targets, not pc.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-e2e-omp-relaxed --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 1.4 — GPU-tail cifar-dense e2e differential (NearEqual)
- **Asserts:** `Schedule { OMP/firstTier 1..k, GPU k+1..9 }`; after drain, per item `NearEqual(kE2eRtol=5e-3, kE2eAtol=5e-3)` vs that item's golden + id-of-output==id-of-input. CUDA = direct §1 managed-mem regression gate **in the concurrent path**; Vulkan = §7 Mali coherency gate.
- **GATE:**
  ```
  CUDA:        scripts/run-on-jetson.sh test-pipeline-e2e-cifar-cu
  Vulkan:      ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-on-rocky.sh test-pipeline-e2e-cifar-vk
  Mali:        ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-mali-oracle.sh test-pipeline-e2e-cifar-vk
  ```

## Category 2 — CPU affinity / tier verification

**Bug class caught:** empty/duplicate tier vectors; big↔little swap in `get_cores_by_type`; whole-tier mask letting the OS collapse all threads onto one core; a kernel migrating off-tier; tier-classification reading `scaling_cur_freq` instead of `devices/*.json`; absent-vs-present-but-unpinnable cores; medium-tier folded onto little.
**Backends:** OMP.
**Priority:** **P1** (binding-disjointness sub-case promoted to **P0** — see 2.1) · **Effort:** S

> Critiques converge: a `sched_getaffinity` mask read-back is **strictly too weak** (setaffinity can succeed while the thread keeps running on its current wrong core until the next reschedule; a short stage finishes before migration). And membership-only sampling passes even if all 8 big threads collapse onto core 0. Both are corrected below.

### Case 2.1 — get_cores_by_type returns exactly the JSON tier set, tiers disjoint  *(P0 — cheap, catches the silent big↔little swap)*
- **Asserts:** Drive ground truth from `devices/pc.json` (not the same globals the loader populated): `get_cores_by_type(kBigCore)` == exactly the JSON big set; `get_cores_by_type(kLittleCore)` == exactly the JSON little set; **disjoint** (no overlap). Assert the chunk's declared `ProcessorType` maps (via `get_processor_type_from_chunk_config`) to the tier whose cores were actually bound. The e2e differential is blind to this swap, so it must be asserted directly.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-affinity-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 2.2 — bind + read-back mask matches device JSON tier
- **Asserts:** For each present tier `T`: `bind_thread_to_cores(get_cores_by_type(T))`; `sched_getaffinity` read-back == exactly the JSON core-id set for `T` (`CPU_ISSET` equals membership, no extra/missing). `GTEST_SKIP` if tier absent. *(Necessary but not sufficient — 2.3 is the real gate.)*
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-affinity-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 2.3 — in-kernel running-core sampling: in-tier AND spread across the tier
- **Asserts:** Inside the actual tree OMP `dispatch_multi_stage(big-cores,…)` on a real `AppData`, each OMP thread records `sched_getcpu()` **repeatedly during the stage body** (add a `sched_yield`/short spin after bind to force a reschedule so a no-op setaffinity is exposed):
  - every sampled CPU ∈ the tier's core set (no off-tier migration), and
  - the **union of distinct sampled cores covers the tier**: `|distinct sampled cores| >= min(num_threads, tier_size)`, and no two threads are permanently stuck on one core. This catches the "whole-tier mask lets the OS collapse 8 threads onto core 0" regression that membership-only cannot.
- Parameterize over **all present tiers** from device JSON (`GTEST_SKIP` only truly-absent ones).
- **GATE:**
  ```
  ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-affinity-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc
  mobile: ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-on-android.sh 3A021JEHN02756 test-affinity-omp   # Pixel 7a: 4 little / 2 med / 2 big
          ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-on-android.sh R5CY21Y3VEV   test-affinity-omp   # Galaxy
  ```

### Case 2.4 — medium tier verified on mobile + 3-chunk big|medium|little e2e
- **Asserts:** On Pixel/Galaxy, a medium chunk binds to **exactly** the JSON medium core-id set, distinct from both little and big (catches `get_processor_type_from_chunk_config` returning `kLittleCore` for a medium chunk, or medium chunks never emitted). Add a `big|medium|little` 3-chunk e2e schedule to the mobile gate.
- **GATE:** `ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-on-android.sh 3A021JEHN02756 test-affinity-omp`

### Case 2.5 — present-but-unpinnable / offline core throws cleanly (no terminate)
- **Asserts:** Bind to a known-unpinnable / offline / `pinnable:false` core id; assert `bind_thread_to_cores` throws a clear `std::runtime_error`, and in the pipeline path the worker try/catch surfaces it rather than `std::terminate`. Cross-check that `pinnable:false` cores are excluded from the tier vectors.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-affinity-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 2.6 — DVFS timing sanity (separate, NON-differential gate — flagged, not folded)
- **Why separate:** A correctness-only differential is **structurally silent** on a big cluster parked at min frequency by governor/thermal — output is identical regardless of clock, but the z3 cost-model premise (big faster than little) is violated.
- **Asserts:** Same tree stage on big-tier vs little-tier wall-time: assert `t_big < t_little` by a margin; on violation, report DVFS/affinity-confused even though correctness holds. **Must not be relied on as part of the differential gate** — documented as a distinct timing harness.
- **GATE:** `ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-on-android.sh 3A021JEHN02756 test-affinity-timing` (mobile, real HW)

## Category 3 — Concurrent CPU+GPU memory visibility (§1/§7 family in the concurrent path)

**Bug class caught:** §1 CUDA managed-mem partial visibility (`concurrentManagedAccess=0`); §7 Mali `HOST_CACHED` stale reads; device-wide-sync-as-accidental-correctness regressing to per-stream async sync; shared-resource `flush_all()`/`invalidate_all()` cross-item clobber; shared-fence aliasing; partial-write hidden on recycle.
**Backends:** CUDA, Vulkan.
**Priority:** **P0** (promoted from P1 — at least one concurrent CPU+GPU case must block GPU PRs; deferring this behind remote-access friction re-creates the exact historical gap) · **Effort:** M

> Critiques converge on a key insight: the single shared `DispatcherT` captured by-ref into every GPU worker means all concurrent GPU items share **one** memory resource and (Vulkan) **one** fence. `vma_pmr.cpp` `flush_all()`/`invalidate_all()` iterate **every** `AppData` buffer in the pool, not the current item's; CUDA uses **device-wide** `cudaDeviceSynchronize()`, not per-stream. A single-GPU-chunk → single-CPU-chunk schedule **never** has two items in the same GPU engine at once, so the cross-item flush/invalidate/fence aliasing is never exercised. Every case below therefore forces **≥2 items in-flight in one GPU engine** with the GPU chunk as the bottleneck.

### Case 3.1 — alternating CPU/GPU boundary, dirty-GPU then concurrent CPU-read  *(P0 gate)*
- **Asserts:** Schedule alternates OMP and GPU chunks so a CPU chunk consumes the **immediately-preceding GPU chunk's `_out`** for the same item *while other items are concurrently GPU-written*. `kPoolSize ≥ 4`, GPU chunk strictly slower than its feeder so its `q_in` backs up (≥2 items in the one engine). Assert per item: `_out == its own golden` (exact/Near) **and** id-of-output==id-of-input. Poison `_out` per cycle; run ≥2 full pool cycles, re-poison between cycles. A stale-cache (§7) or partial-visibility (§1) regression yields zeros/mismatch on a **subset** of items; a cross-item `invalidate_all()` clobber surfaces as a mismatch on the **victim** item.
- **GATE:**
  ```
  CUDA:            scripts/run-on-jetson.sh test-pipeline-visibility-cu      # kPoolSize>=4, GPU bottleneck
  Vulkan(coherent): ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-on-rocky.sh test-pipeline-visibility-vk
  ```

### Case 3.2 — CUDA overlapping {OMP,GPU,OMP}: trailing CPU reads item i while GPU works i+1
- **Asserts:** `kPoolSize ≥ 4`, GPU chunk is the bottleneck; trailing OMP reads item `i`'s GPU output while the GPU is still working item `i+1`. Assert each item `_out == golden` + id match. Distinguishes device-wide-sync-as-accidental-correctness from real per-item correctness; a regression to per-stream async sync corrupts here and is caught. Verify on jetson (`concurrentManagedAccess=0`).
- **GATE:** `scripts/run-on-jetson.sh test-pipeline-visibility-cu`

### Case 3.3 — Mali non-coherent stress, ≥2 items contending one fence (subset-zero + fence-aliasing detector)
- **Asserts:** Same alternating schedule on Mali-G710 phones with the GPU chunk's `q_in` holding ≥2 items so the single dispatcher serializes them through the **one shared `fence_`** under load. Assert: NO item has an all-zero/partially-zero stage output (the exact §7 symptom — `test-tree-vk` s2/s5 returned 0 on Mali); all items match golden topology + id; holds over ≥2 cycles. Catches fence aliasing (item A's `waitForFences` returning on B's signal, or A's `resetFences` clearing B's) driving `invalidate_all()` against the wrong completion point.
- **GATE:** `ssh rocky-ryzen scripts/run-mali-oracle.sh test-pipeline-visibility-vk   # serial across 3A021JEHN02756 (sg16) + R5CY21Y3VEV (sg32)`

## Category 4 — SPSC handoff + reset()/reuse + pool-aliasing race

**Bug class caught:** double-enqueue / pool aliasing (two queue slots holding the same `AppData*`); lost-update/stale-`_out` across recycles; transient concurrent double-touch of adjacent in-place buffers; `next_uid` torn read/lost increment; lock-free `head_`/`tail_` races the differential oracle can't localize.
**Backends:** OMP.
**Priority:** **P1** (no-AppData*-in-two-queues sentinel promoted into the P0 e2e test — see note) · **Effort:** M

> `SPSCQueue` release/acquire guarantees only the **pointer** is visible, not transitive content ordering. `reset()` bumps `uid` only (does NOT clear `_out`). The **sentinel "no `AppData*` in two queues simultaneously" invariant is pulled into the P0 e2e test** (Case 1.1), run under TSan with `kPoolSize=2` for max recycling pressure — the highest-frequency path must not ship without it.

### Case 4.1 — no-loss / no-dup ring invariant under churn (+ id-per-item)
- **Asserts:** Tag each `AppData` with a unique id; assert the multiset of `{ids that exited the last chunk}` == the pool ids each cycle, exactly `kNumToProcess` completions, **id-of-output == id-of-input per item** (not just multiset equality), and no `AppData*` ever appears in two queues simultaneously (owner-tag sentinel). Catches double-enqueue / pool aliasing. (`next_uid` now atomic, so the id keys are sound.)
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-spsc-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 4.2 — TSan clean on the worker/SPSC ring, including next_uid, with TWO concurrent pipelines
- **Asserts:** Build the OMP e2e harness with `-fsanitize=thread`. Run the no-loss/no-dup check with **TWO concurrent pipeline instances** sharing the process (so `next_uid` is hit from >1 thread) and `kPoolSize=2`. Assert ZERO TSan reports across a full `kNumToProcess` run — on `head_`/`tail_` atomics, `AppData` content handoff, **and `next_uid` specifically**. The single-instance harness has exactly one `reset()`-calling thread and would report `next_uid` clean while the real multi-instance path races, so the two-instance variant is required.
- **GATE:**
  ```
  cmake --preset pc -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-fsanitize=thread \
    && cmake --build --preset pc --target test-pipeline-e2e-omp \
    && ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-e2e-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc
  ```

### Case 4.3 — watchdog self-test (deadlock detector validation)
- **Asserts:** Deliberately mismatch counts (one chunk set to expect `kNumToProcess+1`) so a downstream worker spins forever; assert the 30s watchdog **fires** and dumps per-chunk enqueue/dequeue counters, localizing the wedge to a chunk. Validates the detector itself.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-robust-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

## Category 5 — Schedule-execution robustness (absent-PU skip, >kMaxChunks, malformed)

**Bug class caught:** a chunk targeting an absent PU crashing a worker; a schedule with `>kMaxChunks` triggering a Logger OOB throw → `std::terminate`; malformed/non-contiguous (gap/overlap/dropped-first-stage) schedules reaching the executor.
**Backends:** OMP.
**Priority:** **P2** · **Effort:** S

> Only `validate_schedule_coverage` has unit coverage today (`test-schedule-omp`); the executor-level skip and the `>kMaxChunks` survival path are untested.

### Case 5.1 — absent-PU chunk is skipped, not crashed
- **Asserts:** Feed a `Schedule` with a `kSuperCore` OMP chunk on pc (no super tier); assert `schedule_unrunnable_reason()` returns a reason and the executor skips it (process returns cleanly, no terminate). Symmetric: a fully-runnable schedule is NOT skipped.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-robust-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 5.2 — >kMaxChunks schedule does not terminate the process
- **Asserts:** Drive a schedule with >16 chunks through `worker_with_record`; assert the Logger OOB `std::out_of_range` is caught by the worker try/catch (process survives, error logged, ring drains) rather than `std::terminate`. Documents intended degradation.
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-robust-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

### Case 5.3 — malformed schedule rejected before execution
- **Asserts:** Gap/overlap/dropped-first-stage schedules throw from `validate_schedule_coverage` **before** any worker spawns (extends `test-schedule-omp` into the executor entry path).
- **GATE:** `ctest --test-dir build/pc -L omp -R test-pipeline-robust-omp --output-on-failure   # device pc`

## File layout (POC + shared harness)

1. **`builtin-apps/pipeline/pipeline_test_executor.hpp`** — reusable, backend-templated `run_pipeline(...)`. Body mirrors `bm_gen_log_common.hpp` (make_dataset, `std::vector<QueueT> queues(n_chunks)`, pre-fill `queues[0]`, one `std::thread` per chunk running `worker()`, OMP chunk lambda forwards to `omp_dispatch(get_cores_by_type(cpu_pt), cores.size(), *app, start, end)`, join all). **With the three baked-in fixes**: pow2-sized queue + assert all enqueues true; 30s `std::async` join watchdog dumping per-chunk counters; relies on `next_uid` now atomic. Drains the final queue and runs `per_item_check` on what crossed the edge (not the static pool vector). Records last-chunk completion ids into a thread-safe sink. POC keeps it OMP-only (assert all chunks `kOMP`); GPU branch added in Category 3.

2. **`builtin-apps/tree/omp/test_pipeline_main.cpp`** — includes the harness, `tree/omp/dispatchers.hpp`, `tree/tree_diff_oracle.hpp`, `app.hpp`.
   - `AppDataT = tree::SafeAppData` seeded `114514 + i` per pool item; `DispatcherT` trivial OMP dispatcher whose `get_mr()` returns `std::pmr::new_delete_resource()` (mirror `OmpRunner::Mr()`); `QueueT = SPSCQueue<tree::SafeAppData*, 32>` (pow2 ≥ kPoolSize); `omp_dispatch` forwards to `tree::omp::dispatch_multi_stage`.
   - `TEST(PipelineE2EOmp, TwoChunkBigLittle)` — Case 1.1, incl. sentinel-no-aliasing under TSan with `kPoolSize=2`, subset-zero, per-cycle poison + execution-counter, id-match.
   - `TEST(PipelineE2EOmp, PerStageSevenChunks)` — Case 1.2.
   - `TEST(PipelineE2EOmp, RelaxedOrderingStillPasses)` — Case 1.3 negative control.
   - Affinity tier checks (Cases 2.1–2.3) embedded cheaply here for the POC.
   - `main()`: `InitGoogleTest`, `parse_args_test(argc,argv)` (fills `g_big_cores`/`g_lit_cores` from `--device pc`), spdlog off, `RUN_ALL_TESTS`.

3. **`base_appdata.hpp`** — one-line: `next_uid` → `std::atomic<uint32_t>` (`fetch_add` in `reset()`).

4. **`CMakeLists.txt`** (beside the other `bt_add_omp_test` calls, ~line 325):
   ```
   bt_add_omp_test(test-pipeline-e2e-omp builtin-apps/tree/omp/test_pipeline_main.cpp)
   ```
   Links `bt::core + bt::openmp` (carry the tree OMP stage + affinity symbols). If the dispatcher `run_stage_*` symbols aren't already in `bt::core` (match how `test-tree-omp` resolves them), pass the dispatcher source via `${ARGN}`.

## Implementation order

| # | Step | Cases | Backend / gate | Pri | Effort |
|---|------|-------|----------------|-----|--------|
| 1 | Atomic `next_uid` + build reusable `run_pipeline` harness (pow2 queue + assert-all-enqueued + watchdog + completion-edge sink + per-cycle poison + execution-counter + distinguishable seeds + id carry) | — | pc build | P0 | M |
| 2 | **POC:** OMP 2-chunk big\|little e2e differential, incl. id-match, subset-zero, sentinel-no-aliasing (`kPoolSize=2`, TSan), affinity disjointness (2.1) + in-kernel spread sampling (2.3) embedded | 1.1, 2.1, 2.3 | `ctest -L omp -R test-pipeline-e2e-omp` (pc) | P0 | M |
| 3 | OMP 7-chunk per-stage e2e + relaxed-ordering negative control | 1.2, 1.3 | pc | P0 | S |
| 4 | **GPU concurrent visibility (≥2 items / one engine, GPU-bottleneck, ≥2 cycles, poison, id-match)** — wired into the remote per-backend gates so no CUDA/Vulkan PR merges without it | 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 | jetson / rocky / mali-oracle | P0 | M |
| 5 | GPU-tail cifar e2e differential | 1.4 | jetson / rocky / mali | P0 | M |
| 6 | Affinity: JSON-truth bind read-back, present-but-unpinnable throw, mobile medium tier + big\|med\|little e2e | 2.2, 2.4, 2.5 | pc + Pixel/Galaxy | P1 | S |
| 7 | SPSC no-loss/no-dup + id-per-item; two-instance TSan incl. `next_uid` | 4.1, 4.2 | pc (+TSan) | P1 | M |
| 8 | Watchdog self-test (deliberate count mismatch fires the detector) | 4.3 | pc | P1 | S |
| 9 | Schedule robustness: absent-PU skip, >kMaxChunks survival, malformed reject | 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 | pc | P2 | S |
| 10 | DVFS timing sanity — **separate non-differential gate**, documented as silent in the correctness suite | 2.6 | Pixel/Galaxy (real HW) | P2 | S |

**Rationale for ordering:** Steps 1–3 deliver the entire locally-verifiable OMP foundation and the harness every later category reuses, with the two oracle corrections (distinguishable items, assert-on-edge) and three harness fixes (SPSC fill, watchdog, atomic uid) baked in from line one. Step 4 is promoted to **P0** and wired into the existing remote gate scripts so the §1/§7 concurrent-visibility family — the bugs that originally reached production precisely because they hid behind remote-access friction — blocks GPU PRs rather than being deferred to the hardest-to-run tier.
